subtopics.title: Five number summary from data
subtopics.exposition: The five number summary consists of the minimum value, the maximum value and the three quartiles. Equivalently, the five number summary consists of the 0th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 100th percentiles. To find the minimum and maximum of a data set that is already sorted, read off the minimum as the first value and the maximum as the last value. To determine the quartiles, use the percentile formula to find where the median and the quartiles lie in the data set. When the median lies between two values (as with 12 values, between the sixth and seventh), the median is the average of those two values. When the first quartile lies between two values (in the 12-value example, between the third and fourth values), the first quartile is the average of those two values. When the third quartile lies between two values (in the 12-value example, between the ninth and tenth values), the third quartile is the average of those two values. The book writes decimal numbers with a comma as the decimal separator, for example 1.25.

subtopics.title: Draw box-and-whisker plots
subtopics.exposition: The box-and-whisker plot shows the five percentiles of the five number summary. The five number summary and the box-and-whisker plot represent exactly the same information, numerically in the case of the five number summary and graphically in the case of the box-and-whisker plot. Once the minimum, maximum and the three quartiles have been determined, they give the five number summary of the data set, which allows the box-and-whisker plot to be drawn. A box-and-whisker plot can also be drawn horizontally.

subtopics.title: Read summary from plot
subtopics.exposition: In a box-and-whisker plot the box shows the interquartile range, the distance between Q1 and Q3. In a box-and-whisker plot a line inside the box shows the median. In a box-and-whisker plot the lines extending outside the box (the whiskers) show where the minimum and maximum values lie.
